topic: Self-protection scope notes from the RC-110 review
detail: Info-level notes from the three RC-110 security-review rounds: (1) user hook scripts that harness settings point at (~/.claude/hooks/*), shell startup files (~/.zshenv, ~/.zshrc, ~/.bash_profile), Gemini and Codex extension directories and the Homebrew tap formula run code in later sessions and are plain, recognisable writes, but are not protected; (2) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*orch* also protects unrelated launch agents whose name holds 'orch' (com.pytorch...), and writing the LaunchAgents directory itself is refused; narrow to com.orchestrator.* and homebrew.mxcl.orch*.plist if that matters; (3) the '.pub' exclusion meant for ~/.ssh/id_* also applies to write patterns (com.orchestrator.orchd.plist.pub is writable, harmless); (4) a replay judges older revisions with today's protection, so events recorded before RC-110 can show as changed where they wrote a path protected since (documented in daemon.md).
